passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of varying concentrations of a novel antioxidant on the growth rate of cultured human fibroblasts over 72 hours. They used a randomized controlled design with five concentration groups: 0 μM (control), 5 μM, 10 μM, 20 μM, and 40 μM. For each group, cell viability was measured using an MTT assay at 24, 48, and 72 hours. Table 1 summarizes the mean absorbance values (± SD) at 72 hours. The results suggest a dose‑dependent increase in cell viability up to 20 μM, after which the benefit plateaus. These findings may inform therapeutic dosing strategies for antioxidant‑based interventions in wound healing.
stem: Which concentration group showed the highest mean absorbance at 72 hours?
explanation: The 20 μM group had the highest mean absorbance (0.85), indicating the greatest cell viability.
trap: Some students may incorrectly select 40 μM because it is the highest concentration, but its mean absorbance (0.83) is slightly lower than 20 μM.

stem: Which of the following best describes the study's design?

options.A: A controlled laboratory experiment with manipulated concentrations and an untreated control

explanation: Correct: The researchers deliberately set the antioxidant concentration for each group of cultured cells and included a 0 μM control, which defines a controlled experiment. Why the others are wrong: B) A cohort study observes exposures it does not assign. C) A case-control study selects subjects by outcome. D) A cross-sectional survey measures one sample at one time without manipulating any variable.
trap: Calling it an observational cohort study because several groups were compared, when the researchers assigned the concentrations.

stem: Which concentration group had the lowest standard deviation?
explanation: The control group (0 μM) had the smallest SD (0.02), indicating the least variability.
trap: Because 40 μM also has a small SD (0.04), some may incorrectly choose it; however, 0.02 is lower.

stem: Which of the following statements best links the antioxidant concentration to cell viability?

options.B: There is a dose‑dependent increase up to 20 μM
options.C: Viability at 40 μM fell below that of the untreated control
options.D: No effect of concentration on viability

explanation: Correct: Absorbance rose from 0.45 to 0.85 between 0 and 20 μM, then stayed about the same at 40 μM (0.83). Why the others are wrong: A) Viability did not keep rising at 40 μM. C) The 40 μM value (0.83) was far above the control (0.45). D) Absorbance clearly changed with concentration.
trap: Claiming that more antioxidant is always better, ignoring that the 40 μM value (0.83) was not higher than the 20 μM value (0.85).
